reading.body:
Microsoft does not publish MW capacity for individual Azure data center campuses, so the scale of this Quincy facility cannot be read from operator disclosure. The campus is one of Microsoft's oldest hyperscale sites, dating to roughly 2007, and sits within Microsoft's Central Washington region that spans Quincy and East Wenatchee across Grant and Douglas counties. This longevity and regional consolidation suggest sustained strategic importance to the operator's infrastructure footprint.

Washington state has 46 mapped data center facilities, of which only 2 operators publish MW capacity figures. The state's total published capacity is 60 MW. This campus ranks third by published MW in the state, though that ranking reflects only the two operators who disclose figures and does not reflect the Quincy facility's actual capacity, which remains unknown. Most mapped facilities in Washington publish no capacity data.

The Quincy site's significance to AI scaling cannot be assessed from published specifications. Microsoft has chosen not to disclose exact addresses, square footage, or power capacity for this campus, treating individual facility transparency as incompatible with its corporate disclosure policy. Any reading of whether this campus matters to AI compute availability depends on data Microsoft does not release.
